recorded: Hand-authored. No live model produced this run; it is the record of what /iterate-visual must do when three passes are not enough.

items.note: Horizontal gridlines behind twelve bars, and a tick label on every one; no value is read off them.
One comparison, repeated across six weeks: checklist against control.
The title reads 'Retention by signup week and arm', which names the axes rather than the Claim.
The legend in the top right has to be read before either colour means anything.
Both arms carry a saturated categorical colour, so neither is the one the Claim is about.
The two default hues differ in lightness; the bars stay distinct rendered without colour.
The value axis runs 20% to 45%, so a three-point gap looks like a doubling.

passes.revision: Turn the gridlines off, drop the legend, put the control arm in grey and the checklist arm in the accent, and rewrite charts[].title to the Claim sentence.

items.note: Gridlines and legend are gone; what is left is twelve bars, six week labels and a value axis.
Unchanged: one comparison across six weeks.
The title is now the Claim sentence with the two shares in it.
With the legend gone, nothing on the image says which bar is which arm; the Reader has to be told.
Control is grey, checklist is the single accent.
Accent and grey differ in lightness; distinct without hue.
The value axis still runs 20% to 45%.

passes.revision: Set the value scale domain to 0–0.5 and add a layered text mark writing each share above its bar.

items.note: No gridlines, no legend, no border.
Unchanged: one comparison across six weeks.
Unchanged from pass 2.
Twelve labels at this width overlap their neighbours: four of the six week pairs render as one smudged string, so no value is readable.
Unchanged from pass 2.

outcome.next_step: Twelve direct labels do not fit this chart at Reader width, and the validated Vega-Lite subset has no per-row offset to stagger them. Two ways out, and the choice is the Operator's: show the six weeks as two labelled lines instead of twelve bars, so only two labels are needed; or keep the bars, drop the labels and carry the weekly numbers in the Claim's table instead. Three passes is a maximum, so this chart is not recorded as passing and is not rendered into the Finding until one of those is chosen.
outcome.note: Six of seven items pass. The score is not the acceptance test: one failing item returns the chart.
